title: SMC Valid Pullback & Inducement: The ONLY Rule You Need to Know

pullback_definition.llm_summary: A Pullback occurs when Price Takes a Break (pauses) and corrects itself or goes against the trend in the market. It is also known as Correction. It is a temporary dip in a generally upward-trending asset price (bullish) or a temporary rally in a downward-trending price (bearish). Pullbacks are short-term and temporary — market corrects for a short period, then resumes its original direction. The video shows side-by-side diagrams of pullback in bullish market (blue, zigzag upward with small dips) and pullback in bearish market (red, zigzag downward with small rallies). Understanding WHEN a pullback is valid is the core teaching of this video — this validity determines whether an inducement is valid.
key_rules: Pullback = Price takes a break, pauses, corrects against the trend
Also known as Correction (forest correction in market terminology)
Temporary dip in uptrend (bullish) or temporary rally in downtrend (bearish)
Pullback is short-term/temporary — market resumes original direction after correction
Valid pullback knowledge is essential — determines valid inducement

liquidity_sweep.llm_summary: Liquidity Sweep is the mechanism by which institutional traders and banks (Smart Money) execute their large orders. Liquidity sweeps are very Quick and Efficient — the move happens so fast that retail traders cannot catch it without prior knowledge. Smart money leaves footprints at sweep locations. The video explains sweep mechanics using a range-bound market: when market builds a high and low, breakout traders place buy stops above and sell stops below. Banks target the side with MORE orders (larger liquidity pool). For a sell-side sweep: market breaks below the low, collects sell stops, then reverses upward. In candlestick form, a sell-side liquidity sweep appears as a long lower wick on a bullish candle — the wick represents the sweep below the previous candle's low, and the body represents the reversal. A cross (X) mark is placed on the swept side to indicate 'market has done its work here'. The presenter emphasizes that liquidity sweep knowledge is essential for EVERYTHING going forward — inducement validity, order block validation, Fibonacci, corrections, setups, and entries.
key_rules: Liquidity sweeps used by institutional traders/banks to execute large orders
Sweep moves are Quick and Efficient — retail can't catch without knowledge
Smart money targets the LARGER liquidity pool side (more orders)
Low Sweep = Sell Side Liquidity Sweep: market breaks below lows, collects sell stops, reverses up
High Sweep = Buy Side Liquidity Sweep: market breaks above highs, collects buy stops, reverses down
In candlestick form: long lower wick on bullish candle = sell side sweep
In candlestick form: long upper wick on bearish candle = buy side sweep
Cross (X) mark on swept side = market has completed its work there
Liquidity sweep knowledge essential for ALL future concepts: inducement, OB, FVG, entries
Retail trader volume is barely 1-2% of institutional volume — banks drive the market

valid_pullback_rules.llm_summary: Valid Pullback is the SINGLE most important filter in this lecture. The definition: When Price Takes out (Sweeps) the Previous Candle's Low or High, it is a Valid Pullback. In Bullish market: the Low of the Highest Candle must be broken (liquidity sweep) to validate the pullback. In Bearish market: the High of the Lowest Candle must be broken. Three key rules: (1) Next candle must sweep/break the previous candle's low/high, (2) Both Candle Closing (body base sweep) AND Liquidity Sweep (wick base sweep) validate the pullback, (3) It is NOT necessary that the next candle must also close or break the HIGH of the previous candle — only the low/high sweep matters. The video demonstrates with detailed candlestick diagrams for bearish market: single candle base (Lowest Candle → next candle breaks its high → valid checkmark), two candle base (same rule → valid), three+ candle base (candles 5,6,7,8 → Lowest Candle's high NOT broken → INVALID X mark), and the tricky A,B,C,D case where you must identify the ACTUAL lowest candle (D, not C) to correctly assess validity. Same logic applies to bullish market (Highest Candle's low must be broken). Critical insight: candle color (bullish/bearish) does NOT matter — only the candle's POSITION as highest or lowest matters.
key_rules: Valid Pullback = When price sweeps the previous candle's Low (bullish) or High (bearish)
Bullish Market: LOW of the HIGHEST candle must be broken by next candle
Bearish Market: HIGH of the LOWEST candle must be broken by next candle
Body close (body base sweep) OR wick sweep (wick base sweep) — BOTH validate pullback
NOT necessary for next candle to also break the high/low in opposite direction
Step 1: Find the HIGHEST (bullish) or LOWEST (bearish) candle in the pullback
Step 2: Check if the next candle(s) broke its low (bullish) or high (bearish)
If broken → VALID pullback. If not broken → INVALID pullback
Inside bars (candles within a larger candle) have NO significance — they don't break high or low
Candle color (bullish/bearish) does NOT matter — only position (highest/lowest) matters
Tricky case: with multiple candles, must find the ACTUAL lowest/highest (may not be the obvious one)

valid_inducement.llm_summary: Valid Inducement is the culminating concept that ties pullback validity to inducement. Definition: Inducement is the first Valid Pullback on the left side of the recent High or recent Low. It is a trap before an area of POI (Point of Interest = Order Block / Supply / Demand zone). The KEY rule: For inducement to be valid, the underlying pullback MUST be valid first. Process: (1) Find the highest point, (2) Look on its LEFT side, (3) Find the FIRST pullback, (4) Check if that pullback is valid using the candle rules, (5) If valid → that's the inducement. If NOT valid → skip it and look for the next valid pullback on the left — THAT becomes the inducement (inducement shifts). The video demonstrates with a candlestick chart showing two 'Highest Candle' labels — the upper one's pullback is INVALID (X mark, 'Valid Inducement? → No') because the highest candle's low wasn't broken. The inducement shifts to the lower swing's pullback which IS VALID (checkmark, 'Valid Inducement? → Yes') because the highest candle's low was broken. A second example confirms the same principle. Critical practical impact: what looks like an Order Block at an invalid inducement is actually a Smart Money Trap — neither the FVG nor OB at that point are tradeable. Understanding this improves success rate from 50% to 80% but reduces total entries from 100 to 70 (acts as a quality filter). Inducement transfer mechanics covered in next lecture (V04).
key_rules: Valid Inducement = FIRST Valid Pullback on left side of recent High or Low
Inducement is a trap before an area of POI (Order Block / Supply / Demand)
For inducement to be valid, the pullback MUST be valid first
Process: Find highest point → look left → find first VALID pullback → that's the inducement
If first pullback is INVALID → skip it → find next valid pullback → inducement SHIFTS there
What looks like an Order Block at invalid inducement = Smart Money Trap (NOT tradeable)
FVG and OB at inducement points are part of inducement zone — NOT tradeable
Understanding valid inducement: success rate 50% → 80%, but entries 100 → 70 (quality filter)
Sell condition: find inducement using LOWEST candle rules, entry BELOW inducement
Buy condition: find inducement using HIGHEST candle rules, entry BELOW inducement
Next lecture (V04) covers: how and why inducement transfers from one point to another
